annotations.text: PANORAMIC VIEW OF Mt Morgan, QENENZAND. The directors of the Mount Morgan mining Coy have decided to cease operations and go into voluntary liquidation. There are millions of tons of low grade ore still awaiting treatment, but the management declares that poor prices and high wages make economical working impossible. A large amount of English capital is invested in the mine. The town of Mt Morgan has a population of 10,000. The majority of the business people will be ruined if some mutual arrangement is not made at the eleventh hour between management and the employees, to keep the industry going.

People who live in the heart of Sydney have been kept awake o' nights by the striking of the Post Office Clock. So many have been the complaints from residents and visitors - particularly the latter - that the authorities have invented a 'muting' device, which prevents the chimes from sounding during the night hours. At 6.a.m. the invention which is worked by electricity a automatically starts the chimes going again.

BUSHRANGING IN 1924 Claude Batson, of Jingellic, on the Murray River the border between New South Wales and Victoria, suddenly took to a life of bushranging, and shot four people picnicating on the grass, in the bush on the New South Wales side of the Murray. He was a crack shot, and one of the victims of his deadly aim, died from shots which lodged in his back, and for a whole week all the men from the district about Jingellic, and Holbrook, turned out in thrilling man hunt. Discarding his rifle, and his clothes, Batson swam the Murray into Victoria, and there raided a farm house, where he stole a coat, and a pair of riding breeches, and escaped, bare footed, and without food, into the bush. At last, after suffering privations and perils, he struggled into the barn at the bak of a farmhouse, in search of milk, but was seen entering by two lads employed at the farm. They ran up and seized him, for he was too weak to resist, but cried out in terror. However, he surrendered, and collapsed, for the suffering had told its tale on even his iron frame, and the bush which he had conquered so long, for he was an expert bushman, had won out. The photograph, which was taken immediately after the capture, shows the outlaw, Claude Batson, with his first cigarette after he surrendered.
SYDNEY HARBOR COLLIERY. The Sydney Harbor Colliery at Balmain and the workings extend for a considerable distance under the Harbor. Photo shows first shift coming off duty.

GIGANTIO SEWER SCHEME: Tunnelling through solid rock 300 feet below the ground and the laying of huge concrete pipes across the bed of the harbor are some of the jobs that had to be tackled in the construction of the second ocean outfall sewer, to drain the northern portion of Sydney. The work is nearing completion. Photo shows the electric train that runs through the sewer tunnel for miles.

STATE MINES DEPARTMENT testing samples of coal from Warragul (Victoria), The discovery of a seam of coal 3ft. 6in. thick was recently made on some property owned by a syndicate, and the coal is said to be equal in quality to the best Maitland (N.S.W.) coal. Mr. J.C. Watson, the Department's chief chemist, is second from the left.

THE WOODLE RABBIT is yearly in greater demand for its skin owing to the decreased rigidity of fumes from northern climes. Sheep men and fumes in Australia are glad to see this demand increasing as it helps to rid than of a severe pest. GIGATTIC SEWER SCHEME. Tunnelling through solid rock 300 feet below the ground and the laying of huge concrete pipes across the bed of the harbor are some of the jobs that had to be tackled in the construction of the second ocean outfield sewer, to drain the northern portion of Sydney. The work is nearing completion. Photo shows the size of the concrete pipes used to take the sewer under the harbor. They are cast on the shore on one side, "launched" and then fixed by divers.
SYDNEY'S UNDERGROUND RAILWAY: The earth is being filled in over the Hyde Park underground station, which is now practically completed.
"PLANE LIKE A BAT....WORKED BY FOOT FROM BICYCLE SADDLE SEAT."
AN INVENTOR'S AMBITION。

It seems that the age of the Bird Man is rapidly approaching if the expectations of a young inventor, Mr. H.S. Dixon, late of the Australian Air Force, come true. Mr. Dixon, who is 34, has for many years dreamt of the day when men shall strap wings to their backs and fly like the birds at will, and he believes that within a year or two he will be able to make this possible. Out of the Unemployment dole he has managed to buy materials for the construction of a 30ft. self-propelled pb aeroplane which in appearance is exactly like a gigantic bat. The curved planes which are manipulated by foot pedals move up and down like a bird's wing and the seat is an old bicycle saddle. Pressure on the pedals depresses the planes after atmospheric pressure has elevated them and the weight of the passenger is distributed by means of an ingenious arrangement of elastic springs.
Photo shows...Mr. Dixon, the inventor, in his living quarters in a shed.

Une Mine de Charbon sous la Mer.

Sydney, la florissante capitale de la Nouuelle-Galle-du-Sud, offre cette particularité que les vapeurs qui partent de son port peuvent faire leur plain de charbon avec de lahouille extraite... sous leurs quilles!
En d'autres termes, Sydney et son vaste port ont pour fondations une couche carbonifère qui produit de la houille d'excellente qualité, et que l'on recommence à exploiter.
A la suite d'une explosion de gritou qui aient entraîné l'éboulement d'un puits et de ses galleries, lahouillère aît été abandoned en 1917. La guerre empêchaît les travaux de repération.
La mine, connue sous le nom de Sydney Harbor Colliery (Houillère du Port de Sydney),>vient d'être rouverte. Le puits d'accès, dont notre photographie montre l'entree, a une profondeur de 950 mètres.

Les galeries, dont la longueur totale est de 3.567 metres, s'étendent toutes sous la mer. Assurément, c'est le cas de plusieurs mines de la Mer d'Irlande. Le point interessant ici, c'est que l'entree du puits d'exploitation se trouve sur un quai de l'une des villés les plus riches du monde.

ENTERING A CHAMBER OF DEATH: An experiment of world-wide interest is being tried at the Bellbird Colliery, Cessnock, New South Wales. The colliery caught fire eight months ago, after an explosion, and was sealed up. Many miners were killed and the bodies of six had to be left in the working.s. The seal has now been broken, and the mine entered for a short distance, which is being increased daily. The mine is full of deadly gas which will not sustain life for a fraction of a minute. Volunteers are going into the mine through an air-lock carrying their own air by means of Proto-apparatus. As the admission of air into the mine may cause a terrific explosion, the air lock is being gradually moved into the tunnel as the exploration advances. Photo shows:- A group of the volunteers emerging from the mine after the first entry. Their Proto-apparatus worked excellently.
